text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants (exact, whitespace_case, punctuation, changed_quantity, added_negation, removed_negation, reordered, paraphrase) for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Kaleva Camp case management team registered 412 new protection cases, of which 38 percent involved unaccompanied or separated children. Caseworkers completed follow-up visits for most households within fourteen days of registration. Community volunteers accompanied caseworkers on 120 home visits in the eastern blocks. However, the team did not meet its target for referrals to specialised psychosocial services, largely because the Amari Counselling Unit was closed for six weeks in August. No case files were stored outside the locked cabinet at the field office, and an internal audit in September found zero breaches of data protection rules. The team recommends recruiting two additional female caseworkers before the next reporting period.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Lumen Evening Literacy Network. Each class meets twice a week for 90 minutes, and most groups have between eight and fifteen learners. Volunteers should arrive at least 20 minutes early to arrange chairs and check the lamps. Learners read aloud to volunteers during the first half of each session. Please do not correct every mistake while a learner is reading, because constant interruption discourages beginners. In our 2022 survey, 64 percent of learners said that encouragement mattered more to them than speed. Never take attendance registers home; they must stay in the blue box at the venue. Volunteers who miss three sessions in a row will be contacted by their area coordinator.

variants.punctuation: Never take attendance registers home, they must stay in the blue box at the venue.

variants.reordered: Volunteers read aloud to learners during the first half of each session.
variants.paraphrase: Nearly two-thirds of learners surveyed in 2022 said being encouraged mattered more to them than reading quickly.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023 school year, the Becas Alba programme supported 236 girls attending secondary school in the Valle Serrano region. Scholarships covered tuition, uniforms and a monthly transport allowance of 25 dollars. Ninety-one percent of scholars were promoted to the next grade, compared with 74 percent of girls in the same schools who did not receive support. Mentors met scholars every fortnight to review attendance and study plans. Only four scholars left school during the year, and none of them left because of fees. Two partner schools in Río Claro did not submit end-of-year grades on time, so their results are estimated in this report. We thank the Hollis Foundation for its continued trust and flexible funding.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Tumaini Home Visits programme covered the period from March 2022 to August 2023. Evaluators interviewed 58 caregivers and 112 clients across three wards of Mbesa district. Trained caregivers visited clients at least twice a month, and 87 percent of clients reported taking their antiretroviral medicine without missed doses in the previous week. Clients did not always disclose side effects during visits, particularly when relatives were present. The supply of home care kits was never interrupted for more than ten days. However, caregiver stipends were paid late in five of the eighteen months reviewed. Evaluators recommend private consultation space and a fixed payment date for stipends.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Sahelia Seeds for Resilience project distributed drought-tolerant sorghum and cowpea seed to 1,350 farming households in Kerou and Dunebi communes. Field monitors visited a sample of 210 plots after the first rains. Average sorghum yields on monitored plots reached 1.4 tonnes per hectare, up from 0.9 tonnes in the baseline year. Farmers in Dunebi did not plant cowpea on time because seed deliveries arrived three weeks late. Lead farmers trained neighbours in water-harvesting techniques such as zai pits and stone bunds. No pesticide use was recorded on demonstration plots. The project will expand seed fairs to a third commune next season.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the second term of the 2023–24 school year in 46 primary schools in Ndali district. Cooks served a hot midday meal of rice, beans and fortified oil on 52 of 58 scheduled school days. Meals were not served on the remaining six days because the warehouse in Kossa ran out of beans. Average attendance rose to 89 percent, compared with 81 percent during the same term last year. Parent committees supplied firewood and fresh vegetables in most schools. No cases of food poisoning were reported. Monitors noted that handwashing stations in eleven schools did not have soap during spot checks, and head teachers have been asked to correct this before the third term.

passages.source_passage: This guide prepares volunteers for the Saathi Matri outreach days in Dharavali block. Each outreach team visits two villages a week and should register every pregnant woman it meets. Women should attend at least four antenatal check-ups, yet last year only 47 percent of registered women in the block did so. Volunteers must never give medicines, injections or advice that contradicts the clinic nurse. Nurses examine women while volunteers record blood pressure and weight in the green card. If a newborn is not feeding within the first hour, call the nurse immediately. Remind families that a baby should be kept warm and not bathed for the first 24 hours.

passages.source_passage: During the Lindo Nets campaign week, each distribution volunteer will work at one of 32 fixed sites across Mawele district. Households receive one long-lasting insecticidal net for every two people, up to a maximum of four nets. Do not hand out nets to anyone without a voucher from the registration team. Volunteers should demonstrate how to hang a net before families leave the site. In the 2021 campaign, a follow-up survey found that 30 percent of nets weren't hung within a month. Families should air new nets in the shade for one day, not in direct sunlight. Team leaders collect tally sheets at 4 p.m. and check them against the voucher stubs.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Afya Karibu district health programme found steady progress in Lomaji District since the programme began in July 2021. The district now has 284 active community health workers, against a target of 300. Supervisors visited community health workers at least once a quarter in 9 of 12 sub-counties. Stock-outs of malaria test kits were reported by 22 percent of workers in the last six months. Community health workers did not receive their monthly incentive on time in the first year, which contributed to the resignation of eighteen workers. Household registers were complete and legible in most sampled villages. The evaluation team recommends that the district health office take over payroll by mid-2025.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Pamoja Savings Circles programme formed 64 new village savings and loan associations in the hill villages of Mvumo, bringing the total to 191 groups. Women made up 78 percent of the 4,620 members. Members saved an average of 3,400 shillings per month and borrowed mainly to buy livestock and pay school fees. No group reported a loan default rate above five percent at share-out. Facilitators trained group treasurers to keep the cash box ledger, and treasurers now train new facilitators during induction. Two groups in Mabanga did not complete their annual share-out because of a dispute over a missing key. We are grateful to the Ferrand Trust for funding a second year of field facilitation.
